messages:
Sasha (eng-platform): quick RFC follow-up — thinking about making dashboard panels fully async (separate query workers + result cache) instead of the current sync spinner model. want to call out tradeoffs before i draft a PR.
Priya: sounds good. high level: what problem are we solving first? latency tail? front-end CPU? server cost?
Sasha (eng-platform): main drivers: 1) dashboard load spikes kill API pods (query layer overload). 2) permission checks add 200-400ms to each panel, causing cascading load. 3) heavy panels regularly time out and stall the whole page.
Jordan: +1. We chatted about materialized panel results last month. async workers + TTL cache would let us serve most panels from cache and rehydrate in background. downside: staleness and more infra.
Luca: also need to think about RBAC. If panel queries are materialized across teams, we must ensure query results are filtered/encoded per-access, otherwise leakage risk.
Sasha (eng-platform): exactly. three options i sketched: 
  A) per-user cached results (safe, high cardinality, memory heavy)
  B) per-team cached results + runtime filter (cheaper, requires strong filter correctness)
  C) cached query artifacts (serialized rows) + reapply RBAC per-request (compute cost on read)
Which seems most realistic for our traffic profile?
Priya: B seems cost-effective for orgs, but how many panels are team-specific vs user-specific? we should sample telemetry.
Jordan: telemetry: ~70% of heavy panels are org-level metrics (billing, usage) ; ~20% are user-specific (saved views), rest are tiny. so B looks promising.
Luca: B still needs deterministic filters. Query layer currently does predicate pushdown for RBAC — we must guarantee the same predicate is applied when serving cached rows. cache key must include effective-permset-id.
Sasha (eng-platform): good point. propose cache key = sha(query_normalized + perms_hash + time_bucket). time_bucket = 30s for live panels, 5m for lower-priority.
Priya: how do we compute perms_hash? recomputing full ACL on every cache lookup could be expensive. can we use token-scoped role id + team id?
Jordan: suggestion: maintain a small permset service that computes a stable permset id for a (user, org, route) tuple and updates only on role changes. permset id can be cached in frontend cookie + short TTL in backend.
Luca: note: permset changes are relatively rare, so permset id invalidation on role-change events is feasible. Need audit trail though.
devops-bot: deploy status: query-worker-experimental image pushed to staging (tag: qworker-2026-03-19). runbook: monitor query-latency and mem-usage.
Sasha (eng-platform): operational concerns: autoscaling. if workers become the hot path, we need bounded concurrency per-worker and circuit-breaker back to sync path. fallback = run query on main query layer with lower priority.
Priya: also consider progressive rollouts. start with panels in /org/console/* for internal teams only. measure cache hit rate, tail latency, and error modes.
Jordan: testing suggestions: create a synthetic load that mimics 10% heavy-panel traffic and validate that main query-layer p95 drops by ~40%. also test permset rotation to ensure no auth leakage.
Luca: security: run threat model for cached artifacts: encrypted at rest + key-per-org? probably too heavy. maybe HMAC the cache payload with perms_hash so accidental cross-org reads are detectable.
Sasha (eng-platform): ops cost estimate: additional k8s deployment (3 replicas), redis cluster for cache (small), permset service (1-2 pods). rough monthly cost: +$3-5k on staging->prod.
Priya: long-term refactor idea: push policy-aware filtering down into the compilation layer (query planner) so cached results are canonical and replayable across versions. big lift but better consistency.
Jordan: agree — would also help with snapshot testing of dashboards.
Sasha (eng-platform): next steps i'll do: 1) create RFC PR with architecture diagram + cache key proposal + invalidation. 2) prototype qworker + permset service in staging. 3) run 2-week experiment on internal org.
Luca: include a small compatibility matrix for RBAC models (role-based, attribute-based) in the RFC.
Priya: please tag me + security when PR is up. also add metrics we will track (cache hit rate, p95 query latency, failed-auth incidents).
Sasha (eng-platform): will do. thanks all.
Jordan: thanks — happy to help on load test harness.
Priya: :thumbsup:
Luca: :+1:
Sasha (eng-platform): (closing) will post RFC link in #eng-platform when ready.
